description.narrative:
The new development cooperation strategy “The World We Share” constitutes a basis on which to renew and strengthen development research. It focuses Danish international development cooperation on the promotion of democracy and human rights (of girls and women in particular), on the struggles against poverty and inequality (including conflicts, “irregular migration” and “fragility”) and on the need to tackle the causes and consequences of global warming in the context of improved environmental management and enhanced biodiversity. Wide-ranging partnerships underpin the plans for 2021-25, including with research institutions.
In addition to the more traditional research collaboration projects funding by Danida, a new program providing support for capacity development and research with selected African universities will be designed. The three phases of the BSU program have shown that there is considerable interest amongst Danish researchers and Danish Universities for partnerships with African higher education institutions. Furthermore, the outcomes of the program have been rated highly, both in the 2019-20 evaluation and in the 2021 mid-term review of BSU III, and it appears to have resulted in improved quality education and research at the targeted universities. The BSU program has been unique compared to most other international cooperation aiming at better and more research, because of its consistent focus on developing the capacity of the universities to carry out research-based teaching, do research, and reach out to societal actors. Most other programs focus either on research proper, or on offering PhD or master degrees to individuals. The BSU focus on both research administrative and support aspects, curricula development that embeds research in postgraduate teaching, and on building up research organisations at institutional level which can act as models beyond the chosen scientific theme, and which has outreach built into the approaches to research, must be continued in the new program.
Design of the new capacity development program will be carried out in 2022 with a view to approval of a grant in early 2023 for the period 2023-26. A partnership mapping process will be undertaken, focusing on universities in Uganda, Tanzania, Kenya and Somaliland. Climate change, environment and health will be the thematic focus areas included in the new program
